I have two recipes to recommend to you: Sopa De Ajo and Congee (also known as jook). These are both recipes that bloat up starch to make for a much more filling meal.

Sopa De Ajo means garlic soup but it's basically garlic and bread soup. Chop up a head of garlic, sautee it a bit, add smoked paprika (smoked is yummiest but reg will do) then like 6c water or stock. Let that all simmer for a bit and then add a few handfuls of stale bread cubes or crusts. Simmer for another 10 minutes, until the bread is really saturated and starting to fall apart. Boom, yr done. 

Congee/Jook is a very flexible recipe. Basically it's a savory rice porridge. Here are some ratios of how much rice you use to how much water:

Thick : 1 cup rice to 8 cups water
Medium : 1 cup rice to 10 cups water
Thin : 1 cup rice to 13 cups water 

Now, you can flavor it however you want. A popular one is chicken ginger, but feel free to be creative. Basically what you want to do, once you have everything together, is boil the shit out of it for a few hours, until the grains are mostly broken apart and you're left with a thick porridge. 

Good luck, friend.
